title: Performance canary: automated detection for latency/throughput regressions and rollout guards
author: Priya Singh
release_notes: Adds an automated performance canary detector and rollout-guard policy. Enables automatic rollback on detected latency/throughput regressions and exposes dashboards and alerts. Backwards compatible configuration with safe rollout defaults.
description: Context: We need continuous protection against regressions introduced by model, runtime, or infra changes. This PR implements an automated performance-canary detector integrated into the perf-canary pipeline and adds rollout guard policy primitives used by the orchestrator. Motivation: reduce incidents caused by subtle latency/throughput regressions that only show up under load or specific sequence-length distributions. Summary of changes: 1) new perf-canary/detector service that consumes time-series metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, queue depth) and runs rolling statistical tests + hysteresis to identify regressions; 2) rollout guard controller that can pause/rollback canary rollouts when the detector signals a regression; 3) Helm chart and Kubernetes manifests to deploy the detector as part of redwood deployments; 4) observability additions: dashboards, alerting rules, and tagging to link canary runs to Linear items; 5) CI & e2e harness to simulate regressions and verify rollback behavior. Design references: linear/ENG-3421 and docs/design/perf-canary-auto-detection.md. Implementation notes: - Detector uses a configurable window and baseline selection (baseline can be pinned model-version or rolling baseline). - Detection algorithm combines change-point detection on p95 with throughput drop detection; thresholds include hysteresis and minimum sample count to reduce flapping. - Rollout guard supports canary policies: max-latency-delta, min-throughput, cooldown-period, and auto-rollback flag. - Integration with smart routing: when rollback occurs, requests are routed back to the pinned model variant and traffic-steering adjustments are recorded for audit. Testing and CI: unit tests for statistical logic, integration tests that inject synthetic metric traces, and an e2e pipeline that runs a simulated canary and asserts rollback on regression. Backwards compatibility: config defaults to opt-in for legacy clusters; operators can enable via chart values. Rollout plan: stage in non-prod, then gradual rollout to production starting at 5% traffic for 24h observation window. If the detector observes a confirmed regression, the rollout guard will automatically revert traffic and create a Linear incident (ENG-3590) and an audit log entry. Checklist: - [x] Detector service implemented - [x] Helm chart + k8s manifests added - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Dashboards and alerting rules added - [x] Ops runbook and playbook updated - [x] Linear tickets linked

notes: This change is intentionally conservative: auto-rollback is enabled only when confidence >= 0.95 and minimum sample count is met. Operators can tune thresholds. We should monitor false-positive rate for the first 2 weeks.
audit_summary: All rollback actions create an audit-log entry and a Linear incident; RBAC checks enforced for detector-to-orchestrator calls.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover algorithm edge cases; integration tests simulate both regressions and benign noise; e2e verifies end-to-end rollback path using synthetic traces. Observed auto-rollback in staging during simulation.
user_impact: Low: rollout defaults to opt-in and staged. When enabled, customers may see canary rollbacks which revert to baseline model if regression is detected. This prevents wider exposure to degraded performance.
